speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) to what extent the policy of using Past Reserves to fund land reclamation will be applied to finance the projected $100 billion cost of climate change protection measures announced by the Prime Minister; and (b) what are the roles of the President and Parliament in approving or overseeing the use of Past Reserves for land reclamation-related climate change protection measures.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Parliament debates and approves the Supply Bill every year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Under the Supply Bill, the Government seeks approval for development expenditure, which includes land reclamation costs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The Government provides the President with a statement on land-related expenditures annually.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) will continue to study equitable and sustainable ways to finance the full suite of climate adaptation measures we need to protect our island.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: My understanding would be that when the Supply Bill is passed each year as part of the Budget, the policy then will be that any land reclamation cost will be clearly listed in that year's Budget.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The cost of that will be taken from the Past Reserves and, therefore, will not be required to come from current tax expenditure.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: In the future, when the value of that land will be realised, it will be passed back to Past Reserves.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: So, in other words, is the commitment then, that in all such cases, the cost of land reclamation will be coming from the Past Reserves without a drawdown or the requirement to raise taxes currently, or is it going to be flexible based on the Finance Minister at the time?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And that is the basis for which we operate currently.
